target: docs/annotation-context-patterns.md (part of the bearer): leaf bipinnate (FLOPO:0991014) + pinnule (FLOPO_0985028) pinnatifid (FLOPO:0991078)
reason: Bipinnate with the ultimate segments pinnatifid: two existing values, the second on a part of the leaf. No single term needed.

target: new: position of the widest part
reason: 'Broadest from middle to base' gives a range of positions for the widest part of the blade. It is not one shape value; broadest below the middle would be ovate (FLOPO:0991024).
Close-set veins and bracts sit close to others of their kind without being joined. FLOPO:0991190 already has the synonyms close and closely spaced.

target: new: timing of appearance relative to another organ
reason: Coetaneous (flowers appearing with the leaves, as opposed to precocious or hysteranthous) relates when one organ appears to when another does. It needs the other organ and a time relation, not a unary quality.

target: new: conjunction of two values (flattened PATO_0002254 and ovate PATO_0001891)
reason: Both values hold together: ovoid (EXACT synonym of PATO ovate) and flattened. It is not a continuum and not a new shape.

target: docs/odp/09-relation-to-another-part.md (concealed by PATO_0002516 towards scale leaf PO_0006003)
reason: A relation to another part: the sheaths of orchid pseudobulbs, stems and peduncles are cataphylls. 'Covered' alone was rejected in the previous review for lacking this second term.
A compound of two shape values, read as a continuum. The bearer 'spur' is wrongly mapped to short shoot (PO_0004701); it is the floral spur.
Dark cherry red is a dark red; 'cherry' adds no distinction that PATO can carry.

target: docs/annotation-context-patterns.md (region of the bearer): centre of the bearer + low brightness (PATO_0000327)
reason: A colour of one region, the centre of the scales, not of the whole bearer.
A compound of two shape values, read as a continuum. 'Sub-' is the approximate qualifier (docs/odp/01-approximate-value.md).
'Dirty white' is a vague colour modifier. It is not a quality on its own and has no reliable PATO reading.
Petals or stamens 'all of same length' are a set of like parts that do not differ in size. That is the reading of FLOPO:0991102 equal.
'Same width throughout' means the two sides stay the same distance apart, which is the definition of PATO:0002485.
Flesh-coloured (French 'couleur chair') is a pale pink used for corollas and petals.
It describes leaf pores in what is effectively one source, and pore is a generic part the previous review rejected. Too narrow and unresolved for a term.
A part, not a quality. This follows the rules for 'lateral nerve' and 'primary lateral vein'; 'sans nervures latérales' is then an absence of that part.
Laxly spaced leaves or veins are widely separated from others of their kind. FLOPO:0991189 has the synonyms spaced and widely spaced.
In all examples the leaf's under surface is lighter than the upper, so the leaf's surfaces differ in colour. Unlike the bare 'lighter', the comparison is fixed here.

target: new: conjunction of two values (lyrate FLOPO:0991057 and pinnatipartite FLOPO:0991156)
reason: Both existing values hold together: a lyrate outline that is cut more than halfway to the midrib.
States that leaf scars are present on the twig or stem. The FLOPO anatomy class exists.
The meanings are mixed: a colour overlay ('masked with grayish ochre') and hiding by another part ('masquées par'). Like 'covered', it needs what masks the part.
Filaments or sepals not fused. 'Nearly' is the approximate qualifier of docs/odp/01-approximate-value.md.
Deflexed (bent sharply downward) is read as PATO reflexed, so 'not deflexed' is its negation.
A costa or midvein 'not extending to the apex' ends below the apex, the negation of percurrent. The leaf-cell example ('not extending to the costa') does not fit this reading and should be left out.
A compound of two shape values, like 'linear-lanceolate', handled as a continuum.

target: new: conjunction of two values (acuminate PATO_0002228 and obtuse PATO_0001935)
reason: 'Obtusely acuminate' is an acuminate apex whose tip is blunt. Both values hold, so no new term is needed.
A pedately divided blade. With 3 statements, the existing pedate class is preferred over a separate pedatifid/pedatisect split.

target: docs/odp/09-relation-to-another-part.md (perpendicular to PATO_0002434 towards leaf midvein PO_0020139)
reason: The second term the bare 'perpendicular' lacked is given here. It is a relation to the midrib.
The examples mean different things (lobes turned back, hairs pointing backward, colour pattern reversed). Without context it is not one quality.
A compound of two shape values handled as a continuum. Rhombic maps to rhomboid as in rule C165.
